mainTopic: Whether the airspace above the מזבח counts as the מזבח, after a rejected proof about כלי שרת sanctifying disqualified blood.
overview: This amud begins in the middle of a proof that כלי שרת make even blood received by פסולין fit to be sprinkled from the start. The proof is pushed away, because the משנה may be listing two separate cases. The גמרא then asks a new question: does the airspace above the מזבח count as the מזבח itself? It tries to prove that it does from the rule that the כבש sanctifies like the מזבח, since otherwise nothing could be lifted from the כבש to the מזבח. That proof is answered: the כהן drags the limb up, and the part over the gap follows wherever most of the limb is. From this, רמי בר חמא's question is settled: there is a חיבור for parts going up on the מזבח. רבא בר רב חנן then objects that if the airspace counts, a bird עולה could never be made unfit by intention. רב שימי בר אשי rejects this with a case of intending to take the bird down, adjusted so it works even for רבה. He then begins his own proof that the airspace does count as the מזבח, and that proof is completed on the next amud.

steps.title: A proof from the line about blood received by unfit people
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case of blood that פסולין received and sprinkled. It reads this as meaning unfit people did both jobs. That would imply that if they only received the blood, a fit כהן may sprinkle it from the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה lists an offering 'that unfit people received, and they sprinkled its blood.' Doesn't that mean unfit people did both the receiving and the sprinkling?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a line from the משנה to prove that כלי שרת make even disqualified blood fit to be sprinkled from the start.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists this case among offerings that are not taken down once they are on the מזבח. If 'and they sprinkled' means the same unfit people sprinkled too, then reception alone by פסולין must be a lighter case. The likely reason is that the כלי שרת sanctified the blood, so a fit כהן may sprinkle it in the first place.

keyTerms.meaning: People unfit to do the Temple service
They received the blood in a vessel
They sprinkled the blood on the מזבח
'What, is it not...?': a formula that suggests one reading in order to prove something

phrases.english: [An offering] that unfit people received, and they sprinkled its blood;
What, is it not that unfit people received
and unfit people sprinkled?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי, לָאו שֶׁקִּיבְּלוּ פְּסוּלִין וְזָרְקוּ פְּסוּלִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion of whether כלי שרת sanctify disqualified items to be offered from the start.
steps.raayaObject: That blood received by פסולין may be sprinkled from the start by fit כהנים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's case of 'שקיבלו פסולין וזרקו את דמו', read as one combined case.

steps.title: The line may describe two separate cases
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected. The משנה may mean either case on its own: unfit people received the blood, or unfit people sprinkled it.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It means either that unfit people received the blood, or that unfit people sprinkled it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof by reading the משנה as listing two separate cases instead of one combined case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If reception by פסולין alone is already on the list, the משנה only teaches that such an offering is not taken down once it has gone up. It says nothing about sprinkling it from the start. So the משנה no longer proves that כלי שרת make disqualified blood fit to be offered from the start.

keyTerms.meaning: Or alternatively; here, 'or' between two separate cases

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה can be read as two separate cases, either reception or sprinkling by פסולין. So it does not prove that כלי שרת make disqualified items fit to be offered from the start.

phrases.english: No, [it means] that unfit people received,
or alternatively, that unfit people sprinkled.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא, שֶׁקִּיבְּלוּ פְּסוּלִין. אִי נָמֵי שֶׁזָּרְקוּ פְּסוּלִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the reading used for the proof in step 1.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof from this line of the משנה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It assumed 'received and sprinkled' is one combined case. It can just as well be two separate cases.

steps.title: Does the space above the altar count as the altar?
steps.stepSummary: A new question: is the airspace above the מזבח treated like the מזבח itself?
steps.simpleTranslation: Is the air above the מזבח considered like the מזבח, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about whether the space above the מזבח has the same status as the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Things on the מזבח are sanctified so that they are not taken down. The question is whether something in the air above the מזבח, not touching it, gets the same treatment.

keyTerms.meaning: The airspace above the מזבח
Is considered like, is equal to

phrases.english: The airspace of the altar: is it like the altar,
or not?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲוִיר מִזְבֵּחַ כְּמִזְבֵּחַ דָּמֵי אוֹ לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the previous proof was rejected.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether airspace above the מזבח has the status of the מזבח.

steps.title: Quoting the rule that the ramp sanctifies like the altar
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the משנה's rule that the כבש sanctifies just as the מזבח does. This is the source for the proof that follows.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: just as the מזבח sanctifies, so too the כבש sanctifies.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source to answer the question. This line is setting up the reasoning that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says disqualified items that went up on the כבש are also not taken down. The proof does not come from these words alone. It comes from how items get from the כבש onto the מזבח, which the next step explains.

keyTerms.meaning: The ramp leading up to the מזבח
Sanctifies, so the item is not taken down

phrases.english: Come and hear: Just as the altar sanctifies,
so too the ramp sanctifies.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁהַמִּזְבֵּחַ מְקַדֵּשׁ כָּךְ כֶּבֶשׁ מְקַדֵּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to answer the question in step 3.
steps.raayaObject: That the airspace of the מזבח counts as the מזבח.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה: 'כשם שהמזבח מקדש כך כבש מקדש'.

steps.title: Without airspace counting, nothing could move from ramp to altar
steps.stepSummary: Suppose airspace did not count. Then lifting an item off the כבש would mean it has 'come down' from it, so it could never be brought up to the מזבח. That cannot be right, so airspace must count.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say the air above the מזבח is not like the מזבח, then the air above the כבש is not like the כבש either. How could anyone bring the item from the כבש up to the מזבח? It would already count as having come down!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the proof. If airspace did not count, the rule that the כבש sanctifies would be useless.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To move an item from the כבש to the מזבח, you must lift it into the air for a moment. If the air does not count as the כבש, the item has 'come down' from the כבש, and a disqualified item that came down is not brought back up. Since the משנה says the כבש sanctifies items so they are offered on the מזבח, airspace must count.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And if you say': introduces the opposite view in order to show it fails
Brings up, lifts up
'Descended': it has come down from its holy place

steps.whatToRemember: The rule that the כבש sanctifies only works if the air above the כבש and the מזבח counts like them. Otherwise nothing could ever be moved from the כבש onto the מזבח.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how the גמרא proves a rule by asking whether the opposite view would make an accepted rule impossible to carry out.

phrases.english: And if you say that the altar's airspace
is not like the altar,

phrases.aramaic: אֲוִיר כֶּבֶשׁ נָמֵי לָאו כְּכֶבֶשׁ דָּמֵי;
phrases.english: then the ramp's airspace is also not like the ramp;
how could one bring it up from the ramp to the altar?
It would have become 'descended'!
phrases.notes: Once it's lifted into the air, it has left the כבש, and something unfit that came down isn't brought back up.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי אָמְרַתְּ אֲוִיר מִזְבֵּחַ לָאו כַּמִּזְבֵּחַ דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the source in step 4 answers the question in step 3.
steps.raayaObject: That airspace of the מזבח counts as the מזבח.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The logic of the rule that the כבש sanctifies: without airspace counting, items could never be moved from the כבש to the מזבח.

steps.title: The כהן drags it up the ramp
steps.stepSummary: The proof from step 5 is pushed aside: the משנה can be talking about a כהן who slides the item up the כבש without lifting it into the air.
steps.simpleTranslation: The case is where he drags it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the proof from step 5. Maybe the כהן never lifts the item at all. He just slides it along the כבש, so it never leaves the כבש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 argued that lifting an item off the כבש would count as taking it down, unless airspace counts. If the item is dragged and never lifted, that problem never comes up, so the משנה tells us nothing about airspace.

keyTerms.meaning: drags, slides along (without lifting)
the ramp leading up to the מזבח

phrases.english: Where he drags it.
phrases.notes: He slides the limb up the ramp without lifting it, so it never leaves the ramp's surface.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 5.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof that airspace above the מזבח counts as the מזבח.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the item must be lifted off the כבש. The משנה may be talking about dragging it, where nothing is lifted.

steps.title: There is a gap between the ramp and the altar
steps.stepSummary: Dragging does not fully work, because there is an open gap of air between the כבש and the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is open air between the ramp and the altar!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the dragging answer. Even if you slide the item, at some point it has to cross the gap between the כבש and the מזבח, and there it is in the air.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in step 6 needed the item to stay on a surface the whole way up. The small gap means part of the item must be in the air for a moment, so the airspace question comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: airspace, open air
but surely (opens a challenge)

phrases.english: But there is open air
between the ramp and the altar!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא אֲוִיר יֵשׁ בֵּין כֶּבֶשׁ לַמִּזְבֵּחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the dragging answer from step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a dragged item never passes through the air.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The space between the כבש and the מזבח forces the item through open air, so dragging cannot avoid the airspace question.

steps.title: Each part follows where most of it is
steps.stepSummary: While most of the limb is on the כבש, the part over the gap counts as on the כבש. Once most of it is on the מזבח, that part counts as on the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: When most of it is on the ramp, it is like the ramp. When most of it is on the altar, it is like the altar.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the gap problem. The small part hanging over the gap is treated as part of wherever most of the limb is resting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the gap is small, the limb is never fully in the air. The part over the gap follows the majority. So the item moves straight from 'on the כבש' to 'on the מזבח' without ever being judged as 'in the air,' and the dragging answer stands.

keyTerms.meaning: most of it, its majority
like the altar, treated as the altar

phrases.english: Most of it on the ramp: it is like the ramp;
most of it on the altar: it is like the altar.
phrases.notes: "It" is the limb. The small piece over the gap goes along with the bigger part.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the gap challenge of step 7 and saves the dragging answer.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Principle of majority: the minority follows the majority.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The part of the limb over the gap counts as being in open air.
steps.terutzMaskana: The part over the gap goes along with wherever most of the limb is.

steps.title: This seems to settle רמי בר חמא's question
steps.stepSummary: If one part of a limb counts as being where the rest of it is, that answers רמי בר חמא's question: parts of an offering going up on the מזבח are joined together.
steps.simpleTranslation: Settle from this the question רמי בר חמא asked: is there a joining for things going up on the altar or not? Settle it that there is a joining!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices a side result of the last answer. It seems to solve an open question asked by רמי בר חמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רמי בר חמא asked whether all the parts of an offering count as one unit, so that parts not on the מזבח are treated as if they were on it. Step 8 treated the piece over the gap as being on the מזבח because it is attached to the rest. That looks like a clear yes: the parts are joined.

keyTerms.meaning: resolve, settle (an open question)
a joining, counting separate parts as one unit
things that go up onto the altar

phrases.english: Settle from this
the question that רמי בר חמא asked:
is there a joining for things going up on the altar, or not?
phrases.notes: He is asking whether a part that is not on the מזבח counts as on it because it is attached to a part that is.

phrases.english: Settle it that there is a joining!

steps.triggerLanguage: תִּפְשׁוֹט מֵהָא הָא דְּבָעֵי רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a side result from the answer in step 8.
steps.raayaObject: That there is a חיבור for parts of an offering going up on the מזבח.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The rule in step 8 that the part over the gap follows the majority of the limb.

steps.title: Yes, the question is settled
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees: the inference is fine, and רמי בר חמא's question is indeed settled from here.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is no problem; settle it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the side result. There is nothing wrong with it, and רמי בר חמא's question really is answered: there is a חיבור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 could have sounded like a problem for the answer in step 8. The גמרא says it is no problem at all and simply accepts the result.

keyTerms.meaning: it is not difficult, no problem

steps.whatToRemember: The part of a limb over the gap follows the majority, and from this we learn that there is a חיבור for parts of an offering going up on the מזבח.

phrases.english: That is no problem; settle it.

steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רמי בר חמא's question is settled: there is a חיבור for things going up on the מזבח.

steps.title: Challenge from the bird burnt offering
steps.stepSummary: רבא בר רב חנן argues: if the airspace counts as the מזבח, then a bird עולה is already 'caught' by the מזבח when it is killed. How could a wrong intention ever make it unfit?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא בר רב חנן objected: If you say the airspace of the altar counts like the altar, then a bird burnt offering that is made unfit by a wrong intention, how could that ever happen? The altar has already taken hold of it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the main question about airspace. רבא בר רב חנן attacks the idea that the airspace above the מזבח counts as the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A bird עולה has its neck pinched in the air above the מזבח. If that air counts as the מזבח, the bird is 'caught' by the מזבח right away, so even if it is left until tomorrow it is not taken down and may still be burned. A wrong intention only makes an offering unfit when it plans something forbidden. Planning to burn it tomorrow would plan nothing forbidden, yet we know such a disqualification exists.

keyTerms.meaning: objects to it, attacks it
a bird burnt offering
a (wrong) intention during the service that can make an offering unfit
took hold of it, 'caught' it

steps.confusionAlert: רבא בר רב חנן is not asking about the כבש or the gap. He is going back to the main question of whether the air above the מזבח counts as the מזבח, and arguing that it cannot.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רָבָא בַּר רַב חָנָן:
phrases.english: רבא בר רב חנן objected to it:
And if you say the airspace of the altar
is like the altar,
a bird burnt offering that one made unfit by a wrong intention,
how can you find such a case?
The altar has already taken hold of it!
phrases.notes: The bird is killed in the air above the מזבח, so it would already count as on the מזבח.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רָבָא בַּר רַב חָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side point about חיבור and returns to attack the claim that airspace counts as the מזבח.
steps.kashyaTarget: The position that the airspace above the מזבח counts as the מזבח.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the air counts as the מזבח, a bird עולה is caught by the מזבח as soon as it is killed above it, so burning it the next day would still be valid. An intention to burn it then plans nothing forbidden and could not make it unfit, yet we know such a case exists.

steps.title: A case where a wrong intention still makes the bird unfit
steps.stepSummary: רב שימי בר אשי pushes back on רבא בר רב חנן. Even if the airspace counts as the מזבח, a bird עולה can still be made unfit by intention: he intends to take it down tomorrow and then burn it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שימי בר אשי challenged this: Why can't you find such a case? You can, when he says: 'I am doing מליקה on it so that I can take it down tomorrow, and then bring it back up and burn it.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב שימי בר אשי rejects the challenge from step 11. He shows a real case where a wrong intention would still make a bird עולה unfit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא בר רב חנן said that once the bird is 'caught' by the מזבח, no wrong intention could ever matter. רב שימי בר אשי answers that the intention can be to take it down off the מזבח and burn it the next day. Once it comes down the next day, it cannot go back up, so the wrong intention really does have something to make unfit.

keyTerms.meaning: He challenges it (pushes back on the previous statement)
Killing a bird offering by pinching the neck with the כהן's fingernail
With the intention of; in order to
To burn the offering on the מזבח

steps.confusionAlert: רב שימי בר אשי is not saying the airspace does NOT count as the מזבח. He only shows that רבא בר רב חנן's objection does not prove it. A wrong intention can still matter, because the plan includes taking the bird down.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב שִׁימִי בַּר אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Shimi bar Ashi objects to it:
phrases.notes: He is pushing back on רבא בר רב חנן's challenge from step 11.

phrases.english: Why can you not find it?
phrases.notes: Why can't you find a case where a wrong intention makes the bird עולה unfit?

phrases.english: For example, where he says:

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵינִי מוֹלְקָהּ עַל מְנָת לְהוֹרִידָהּ לְמָחָר
phrases.english: I am hereby pinching it in order to take it down tomorrow
and to bring it up and burn it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב שִׁימִי בַּר אָשֵׁי: אַלְּמָה לָא מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the challenge of step 11 by showing a case it overlooked.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבא בר רב חנן's claim that a bird עולה could never be made unfit by intention if the airspace counts as the מזבח.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: He overlooked an intention to take the bird down and burn it the next day. Once it comes down, it cannot go back up.

steps.title: This case only works for רבא, not for רבה
steps.stepSummary: רב שימי בר אשי's case works for רבא, who holds that staying overnight makes an offering unfit even on top of the מזבח. For רבה, who holds it does not, the intention would mean nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well for רבא, who says that staying overnight makes an offering unfit even on top of the מזבח. But for רבה, who says staying overnight does not make it unfit on top of the מזבח, his intention means nothing!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions רב שימי בר אשי's case. It seems to work only for one side of a disagreement between רבא and רבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבא, a bird left overnight on the מזבח becomes unfit, so taking it down the next day really is an unfit plan. For רבה, staying overnight on the מזבח does nothing. So the bird stays fit, and the planned delay would not count as a disqualifying intention.

keyTerms.meaning: This works well (for one opinion, but not for another)
An offering left overnight past its proper time, which normally makes it unfit
Has an effect (here: makes it unfit)
The top of the מזבח
His intention

phrases.english: This works out well according to Rava, who says:
being left overnight has an effect at the top of the altar;
but according to Rabba, who says:
being left overnight has no effect at the top of the altar,
his intention is meaningless!
phrases.notes: Since the bird does not become unfit for רבה, planning that delay is not a disqualifying intention.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא לְרָבָא, דְּאָמַר: לִינָה מוֹעֶלֶת בְּרֹאשׁ הַמִּזְבֵּחַ; אֶלָּא לְרַבָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the case given in step 12 based on רבה's opinion.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב שימי בר אשי's case of intending to take the bird down tomorrow.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The case depends on staying overnight on the מזבח making the bird unfit, which רבה does not accept. So for רבה the intention is meaningless.

steps.title: Even for רבה: taking it down before dawn
steps.stepSummary: Even for רבה there is a case: he intends to take the bird down before dawn and bring it back up after dawn, so it stays overnight off the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even for רבה you can find a case: when he says, 'I am doing מליקה on it so that I can take it down before dawn, and bring it back up after dawn.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב שימי בר אשי answers the question from step 13. He gives a case that works even for רבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה only says that staying overnight on top of the מזבח does not make an offering unfit. If the plan is to take the bird down before dawn, it spends the dawn off the מזבח, and then even רבה agrees it becomes unfit. So the intention has real meaning according to everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: Dawn, when the night ends and an offering left over becomes unfit
To take it down (off the מזבח)
To bring it up (onto the מזבח)

steps.whyThisMatters: After this answer, רבא בר רב חנן's objection is fully rejected according to both רבא and רבה. That opens the way for the proof in the next step.

phrases.english: According to Rabba as well, you can find it:
for example, where he says:
I am hereby pinching it in order to take it down
before dawn,
phrases.notes: So the moment of dawn finds it off the מזבח, and even רבה agrees it becomes unfit.

phrases.english: and to bring it up after dawn.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13 by adjusting the case so it works for רבה too.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changing the case (the bird is taken down before dawn instead of the next day)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The case only works for רבא, because for רבה staying overnight on the מזבח does nothing.
steps.terutzMaskana: If he intends to take it down before dawn, it stays overnight off the מזבח, and even רבה agrees it becomes unfit.

steps.title: A proof that the airspace counts as the מזבח begins
steps.stepSummary: רב שימי בר אשי says that, in any case, we can settle the question one way: the airspace of the מזבח counts as the מזבח. He begins to show what would go wrong if it did not.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any event, settle the question in this direction: the airspace of the מזבח is like the מזבח. Because if you think the airspace of the מזבח is not like the מזבח...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new proof. רב שימי בר אשי says the airspace counts as the מזבח, and starts an 'if it were not so' argument that finishes in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now he only rejected רבא בר רב חנן's objection. Now he goes further and proves the opposite side, that the airspace does count as the מזבח. He does this by imagining the airspace does not count and showing that this leads to a problem, which is spelled out next.

keyTerms.meaning: To this side (in this direction)
In any event; at least
Settle (resolve) the question
The airspace above the מזבח
If it enters your mind (if you were to think)

phrases.english: In any event, resolve it to this side:
that the airspace of the altar is like the altar;
for if it enters your mind
that the airspace of the altar is not like the altar,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting the objection, he turns to his own proof for the opposite side.
steps.raayaObject: That the airspace above the מזבח counts as the מזבח itself.
steps.raayaSupportSource: An 'if it were not so' argument (דאי סלקא דעתך אויר מזבח לאו כמזבח דמי), which is completed on the next amud.
